'''''Viola lactea''''', also known by its common name '''pale dog violet''',<ref>{{cite web |title=Viola lactea/pale dog violet |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/75237/Viola-lactea/Details |website=[[Royal Horticultural Society|RHS]] |access-date=30 July 2021}}</ref> is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Violaceae]].

==Description==
''Viola lactea'' has sparsely hairy creeping stems and a [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]] of [[lanceolate]] leaves which are [[cuneate leaf|cuneate]] at their base. Each stem has one flower; the flowers are shaped similar to [[Viola (plant)|other violets]] and go from milky-violet to greyish-pink in colour, with the deep purple veins on the lower petal. The presence of green spurs at the back of its flower and the triangular [[stipule]]s on its upper leaves being equal or longer in length than the leaf stalks differentiate ''V. lactea'' from other similar species.<ref name="PL">{{cite web |title=Pale Dog-violet Viola lactea |url=https://www.plantlife.org.uk/application/files/5315/4747/7087/Pale_Dog-violet.pdf |website=[[Plantlife]] |access-date=30 July 2021 |archive-date=30 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210730185433/https://www.plantlife.org.uk/application/files/5315/4747/7087/Pale_Dog-violet.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=BFTB />

This species hybridizes easily with ''[[Viola riviniana]]'', which often occurs in the same habitat. The population of hybrid plants is thought to be increasing where both species are present, especially around the [[Geography of Cornwall|Cornish coast]], as the ''V. riviniana x lactea'' hybrid outcompetes both its parent species. However, the hybrid plants are generally [[Sterility (physiology)|sterile]]. ''V. lactea'' can also hybridize with ''[[Viola canina]]'', though this is much more rare.<ref name=BFTB />

==Habitat==
''Viola lactea'' grows on [[heath]]land, and favours areas which are bare or only have short vegetation (due to [[grazing]], burning or other disturbance such as [[Peat|turf cutting]]).<ref name=PL2>{{cite web |title=Pale dog-violet |url=https://www.plantlife.org.uk/uk/discover-wild-plants-nature/plant-fungi-species/pale-dog-violet |website=[[Plantlife]] |access-date=30 July 2021 |archive-date=30 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210730185430/https://www.plantlife.org.uk/uk/discover-wild-plants-nature/plant-fungi-species/pale-dog-violet |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Distribution==
The [[native range]] of ''V. lactea'' is described as [[Western European]] Oceanic. It occurs in the south and west of the [[British Isles]], along the Atlantic coast of [[France]], and in north-western [[Spain]]. Its southern reach is in [[Portugal]], around the [[River Tagus]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=D. M. Moore |title=Population Studies on ''Viola lactea'' Sm. and its wild hybrids |journal=[[Evolution (journal)|Evolution]] |date=September 1959 |volume=13 |issue=3 |pages=318–332 |doi=10.1111/j.1558-5646.1959.tb03019.x |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Within the British Isles, it is now most common in the [[New Forest]], [[Dorset]], [[Cornwall]], [[Pembrokeshire]] and [[County Kerry]]; it is no longer found in much of its previous range (especially in [[South East England]]) due to habitat decline.<ref name=BFTB>{{cite web |title=Pale Dog-violet Viola lactea |url=https://naturebftb.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pale-Dog-violet.pdf |website=Back from the Brink |access-date=30 July 2021}}</ref>

==Protection==
''Viola lactea'' is classed as [[Vulnerable species|'Vulnerable']] within [[Great Britain]] and [[Endangered species|'Endangered']] within [[England]].<ref>{{cite book |author1=P. A. Stroh |author2=S. J. Leach |author3=T. A. August |author4=K. J. Walker |author5=D. A. Pearman |author6=F. J. Rumsey |author7=C. A. Harrower |author8=M. F. Fay |author9=J. P. Martin |author10=T. Pankhurst |author11=C. D. Preston |author12=I. Taylor |title=A Vascular Plant Red List for England |date=2014 |publisher=[[Botanical Society of Britain and Ireland]] |page=31 |url=http://www.surreyflora.org.uk/mbr_docs/00000071.pdf |access-date=30 July 2021 |archive-date=10 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810132238/http://www.surreyflora.org.uk/mbr_docs/00000071.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> It is designated as a species "of principal importance for the purpose of conserving biodiversity" under the [[Natural Environment and Rural Communities Act 2006]].<ref name=PL2 />
